transcript.title: Opening
transcript.text: Good morning Rushil Bhatia. Here is your daily news for Monday, November 16. In today's briefing: top headlines, bhopal and madhya pradesh, business and markets, money, tax and personal finance, science and technology, across india, around the world. Let's begin.

transcript.title: Top headlines
transcript.text: First, the stories leading the news this morning. 'Perfectly safe' but not 'maxed out'? Trump takes Qatar jet to Asia. US President Donald Trump is set to travel to Asia on Monday aboard the aircraft gifted by Qatar, even as questions remain over its promised security upgrades. According to NBC News, the jet has received some maintenance and cosmetic improvements, but the larger overhaul remains unclear months after an Iran-related security scare forced Trump to fly home from Turkey on a secret military plane. I want to win matches for India for a long time: Naman Dhir. In an exclusive conversation with TimesofIndia.com, Naman Dhir spoke about his rapid rise, the challenges of life in international cricket, his bowling transformation, and his dream of featuring in the 2027 ODI World Cup. 10,000+ flights hit by disruption as US air-traffic system remains crippled. US airlines faced significant disruptions as more than 10,000 flights were canceled or delayed due to technical failures. The issues resulted from maintenance work on routers used by the Federal Aviation Administration, leading to widespread communication problems. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy stated that the situation could normalize by Monday, highlighting ongoing challenges with aging technology. Scott Bessent signals 'dramatic shakeup' at Nvidia after Lutnick chip remarks. Following the dismissal of CEO Jensen Huang, U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent advocates for a radical leadership shift at Nvidia. He is demanding Nvidia's board to clarify recent claims about chip exports to China. Stressing the importance of external legal guidance, Bessent points out a pervasive culture of noncompliance within the company. 'Bowlers win you series': Gambhir's message after India's historic triumph. India achieved a 3-1 ODI series victory against New Zealand, highlighted by strong bowling performances. The final match featured India's bowlers dismissing New Zealand for 187 runs while defending a total of 210. Gautam Gambhir praised the team's bowling depth after the win. Despite batting struggles, Shreyas Iyer acknowledged the players' resilience and commitment throughout the series. Mountaineer turns protector for 18 hyenas near Pakhi Pahar. In Purulia, West Bengal, Joydeep Chakraborty has been diligently working to shift the negative narratives surrounding striped hyenas. Starting his field research in 2017, he engaged local communities to foster understanding and reduce harmful practices against these vital scavengers. His efforts have led to the discovery of 18 to 19 hyenas through camera traps, underscoring their presence and ecological importance. Jensen Huang plots Nvidia return; Musk, 158,000 others sign petition backing come back. Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is discussing a return to the company just days after stepping down following revelations of an alleged affair with Alice Huang, a Chinese businesswoman suspected by US of spying for Beijing, and separate alleged relationships with subordinates, the Financial Times reported. PM Modi to attend Asean summit in Manila today; what's on agenda. Prime Minister Narendra Modi will travel to Manila on Monday for a two-day visit to attend the 23rd India-Asean Summit and the 21st East Asia Summit. Oil prices fall as surplus fears return after nine-month dry spell in the market. Oil prices are on a downward trend due to an anticipated surplus and a recovery in shipments through the Strait of Hormuz. The International Energy Agency has indicated that supply could outstrip demand in the upcoming quarter, altering market forecasts. However, the United States has tightened restrictions on oil transport between its ports, complicating shipping logistics, while high freight rates continue to challenge traders amidst these changes. Cong suggests Army 'friendly fire' behind deaths of 2 SPOs in Kishtwar, BJP hits back. In Jammu and Kashmir, Congress has called for a thorough investigation into the tragic killing of two special police officers. Initial reports indicate that the officers may have been accidentally shot by Army personnel during a hunting operation. The BJP has dismissed these allegations, claiming they tarnish the integrity of the security forces. Man who used homemade radar as teen helps uncover 600 lost graves in Australia. Known for his remarkable work, Dave Hunter, 'Dave the Grave Hunter', has made a significant discovery of 658 unmarked graves throughout Australia. His company, Hunter Geophysics, employed ground-penetrating radar to meticulously complete the project in 2026, all while maintaining the integrity of existing cemeteries. Local councils are keen to safeguard these findings and attach stories to each grave. Future endeavors may also reach out to nearby areas grappling with identical predicaments.

Indian women's hockey players Sushila Chanu, Bicchu Devi and Jyoti Singh, trained at Madhya Pradesh's Gwalior Hockey Academy, are confident ahead of the Women's Asian Champions Trophy 2026 in Bhopal. Licence Raj Legacy Still Haunts Corporate Innovation In India, IIM Indore Study Finds 7.9 percent Decline In New Products. An IIM Indore study examining 6,216 manufacturing firms found that prolonged exposure to India's pre-1991 Licence Raj was associated with reduced product innovation after liberalisation. A 21-year-old Indore woman filed a police complaint against a garment shop salesman who allegedly harassed her relatives for her phone number, offering up to rupees 50,000. Indore Police launched Operation Midnight across four zones, checking 1,419 suspects and taking action against 722 people.

Sebi plans AI guardrails for capital markets, focus on investor protection. Markets regulator Sebi will soon issue detailed guidelines for the responsible use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in the capital markets, its chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey said, emphasising the need to balance technological innovation with investor protection. The Sebi chief said the proposed guidelines would focus on establishing appropriate guardrails for AI use, including disclosures, accountability of regulated entities and a 'human-in-the-loop' approach to ensure that critical decisions are subject to human oversight. In June 2025, Sebi floated a consultation paper proposing guiding principles for responsible usage of Artificial Intelligence (AI)/ Machine Learning (ML) applications/models in securities markets. These guiding principles are intended to optimise benefits and minimise potential risks associated with the integration of AI/ML based applications in securities markets to safeguard investor protection, market integrity, and financial stability. FPIs pump rupees 84,290 crore into equities in first fortnight of November. Foreign investors made a strong comeback to Indian equities in the first fortnight of November, pumping in rupees 84,290 crore after two consecutive months of net outflows, amid a global AI sell-off, falling crude prices and attractive large-cap valuations. The latest inflows follow net withdrawals of rupees 34,843 crore in October and rupees 35,861 crore in September, according to data from the depositories. According to the data, Foreign Portfolio Investors (FPIs) made a net investment of rupees 84,290 crore in Indian equities during November 2-13, covering nine trading sessions. With the latest inflows, cumulative FPI outflows from Indian equities have narrowed to around rupees 2.1 lakh crore in 2026 from nearly rupees 3 lakh crore a few weeks ago. Banks adopting artificial intelligence (AI) agents could see their investments pay off in around 10 months and generate returns of nearly three times the initial investment over three years, according to a report by McKinsey, which said the technology could reshape the economics and competitive landscape of the banking sector. Apple's new study looks to improve the effectiveness of AI health tools. Apple announced a new study today with the goal of better understanding how people interact with conversational AI health tools and how useful their responses actually are. The company is conducting the Apple Health AI Usage Study in collaboration with OpenEvidence, a clinical AI platform used by healthcare professionals that generates answers based on medical Apple launches new app to study how people use AI for health. Apple's new app for a study will answer everyday medical questions Vitamin C could help block cancer-linked chemicals in your stomach, study finds. Scientists have discovered that vitamin C may help prevent potentially cancer-causing chemicals from forming in the stomach after eating foods containing nitrates and nitrites. A new mathematical model suggests that taking vitamin C after meals could reduce these harmful reactions, offering a possible new strategy for lowering cancer risk. Listen to this: Armand Hammer's Snakes and Ladders. I open with this caveat: I haven't had a ton of time to digest the surprise Armand Hammer record that dropped this week. Billy Woods and Elucid rarely miss, though, and my initial reaction is that Snakes and Ladders ranks among their best. It doesn't have the seamless throughline production-wise that their collabs with Alchemist Indian chip startup Bharat Semi lands $24M seed round as it eyes global AI sensor market. Bharat Semi says it has secured design wins for its AI-enabled sensor technology with companies including General Atomics. NASA warns this year's Monster El Niño could be even bigger than legendary 1997 event. NASA scientists warn that the rapidly intensifying 2026 El Niño could surpass the historic 1997-98 event, which triggered devastating weather extremes around the world. Satellite data reveal striking similarities between the two, raising the possibility of major rainfall and flooding this winter, although the exact impacts remain uncertain. iPhone 18 Pro versus iPhone 17 Pro versus iPhone 16 Pro versus iPhone 15 Pro Max: Which has the best camera for photography?. From the iPhone 18 Pro's variable aperture to the iPhone 15 Pro Max's 5x optical zoom, Apple's Pro models offer different photography features. Here is how four generations compare on camera quality, zoom, portraits and low-light photography. Vulcan rocket fails, destroying 40 Amazon Leo satellites. United Launch Alliance (ULA) suffered what is reportedly its first mission failure in its 20-year history, failing to deliver 40 Amazon Leo satellites to orbit. Leo is Amazon's competitor to SpaceX's Starlink, but it has struggled to get off the ground so far, putting only a small portion of the necessary satellites to challenge Starlink Is bad news for Jensen Huang also bad news for the AI industry?. "Jensen is Nvidia, right? And so much of this economy is riding on Nvidia." Uranus and Neptune's bizarre magnetic fields may finally be explained. The strange, wildly tilted magnetic fields of Uranus and Neptune have puzzled scientists since NASA's Voyager 2 spacecraft explored the planets in the 1980s. New simulations suggest that extreme conditions deep inside these icy giants create unusual electrical properties that could explain their magnetic fields. Remarkably, the models indicate that their magnetic poles could shift by tens of degrees within just a few decades, far faster than Earth's. Jensen Huang might be plotting a return and more of the latest Nvidia drama. The drama around Nvidia co-founder and former CEO Jensen Huang is evolving quickly. The latest edition of our Stepback newsletter should get you up to speed, but there have already been a number of new developments since this morning. That includes rumors that Jensen Huang might be trying to find a path back to CEO, SNL gathers all the tech tycoons for a lesson in dating and spycraft. While awkward, creepy tech executives have become a recurring theme on Saturday Night Live, this week's episode gave the cast a chance to show off all their impressions at once. Astronomers discover a dead star spinning every 8 minutes and sending mysterious radio pulses. Scientists have discovered a strange stellar pair more than 5,000 light-years away, where a dead star spinning every eight minutes produces mysterious radio pulses while orbiting a Sun-like star. The breakthrough also revealed massive magnetic storms on the companion star, offering fresh clues to one of astronomy's emerging mysteries. Congress wants to tighten export rules on AI chips after Nvidia spy scandal. Unsurprisingly, following the scandal involving now-former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and a suspected Chinese spy, Congress is looking to further restrict exports of AI chips. Both Democrats and Republicans have voiced support for various measures and bills that would tighten rules and have demanded that Huang and other Nvidia leaders testify before Congress. Alzheimer's may start shrinking two brain regions years before memory loss. Johns Hopkins scientists have uncovered hidden warning signs of Alzheimer's disease that may appear up to a decade before memory loss begins. Brain scans revealed that two regions involved in memory and emotion start shrinking before the hippocampus, the area doctors typically examine for signs of Alzheimer's. These early changes are linked to abnormal tau protein buildup and could provide a powerful new way to identify people at risk. GTA 6: Why haven't the game's original creators been allowed to play it before launch?. Despite the excitement surrounding the release, Rockstar Games has kept details of GTA 6 closely guarded. Its strict secrecy extends even to the people who helped create the original game. Fanttik's S1 Pro electric screwdriver is $40 off in the run-up to Black Friday. Amazon's early Black Friday promos are already underway, and we'll be highlighting some of our favorites over the next few days on our Shopping page. Among them is the Fanttik S1 Pro Cordless Electric Screwdriver, which is currently matching its all-time low of $39.99 ($40 off) at Amazon for a limited time. Welcome back to TechCrunch Mobility, your hub for the future of transportation and now, more than ever, the role AI is playing in it. A common osteoporosis drug blocked spinal damage in a surprising new study. Scientists have uncovered a surprising genetic connection to spinal degeneration and found that an existing osteoporosis drug can prevent damaging mineral buildup in zebrafish spines. The discovery could pave the way for new treatments that slow or prevent a major cause of chronic back pain. From Microsoft 365 to CrowdStrike - Biggest tech outages that almost brought the world to a standstill. A Microsoft 365 outage that began November 12 disrupted email and other services for days before being resolved Saturday. It joins a series of major global technology failures in recent years, including incidents affecting Windows devices, Meta platforms, AWS, and Google. Apple's first smart glasses are coming together. Apple's smart glasses are among the worst-kept secrets in the tech world. Bloomberg's Mark Gurman says the company's first model, which will lack augmented reality features, will be announced at June's WWDC next year. transcript.title: Across India
transcript.text: Turning to the big national stories. BJP MP Ajeet Gopchade urges PM Modi to ensure representation of divyang persons in Parliament. Ajeet Gopchade has requested Prime Minister Narendra Modi to develop mechanisms for the representation of divyang persons. He highlighted the successful examples from other countries that facilitate this representation in legislatures. Gopchade suggested that exceptional candidates with disabilities should be considered for Rajya Sabha nominations. The Prime Minister's Office has forwarded his suggestions to relevant ministries for further action. 'No case against me anywhere,' he claims to TOI. Continued from P 1 Lalit gets British citizenship, extradition prospects take a hit. Lalit Modi has announced his acquisition of British citizenship during an event at Oxford Union. While he claims to have faced threats and political persecution, he has refused to return to India. The Enforcement Directorate has ongoing investigations regarding his alleged financial misconduct linked to IPL. Previous requests for his deportation have been denied by the UK government. PM Modi to attend Asean, East Asia summits in Manila; what's on agenda. Prime Minister Narendra Modi will travel to Manila on Monday for a two-day visit to attend the 23rd India-Asean Summit and the 21st East Asia Summit. Security booster for Bachchan, others on Lawrence's target list. Against the backdrop of the Lawrence Bishnoi gang escalating threats against top Bollywood actors, the noose appears to be tightening around the jailed gangster, as investigators have sought his visitors' list from Ahmedabad's Sabarmati Central Jail and are reviewing the security of stars who have recently been threatened or attacked. Ray of hope has reached Gadchiroli this Diwali: PM. Hope has returned to India's erstwhile Maoist heartland where tribal families once despaired at the prospect of armed groups snatching children from their mothers, abducting daughters from their homes and preventing people from even voting, PM Narendra Modi told a gathering in Gadchiroli Sunday as he basked in the "countless blessings" showered on his govt for "defeating Maoism and Naxalism". Government healthcare spend up 3x since 2013-14 to 4.1L cr. Out-Of-Pocket Expense Dips But Families Still Paid 4L Cr In 2023-24 Congress suggests Army 'friendly fire' behind deaths of 2 SPOs, BJP calls it 'provocative'. In Jammu and Kashmir, Congress has called for a thorough investigation into the tragic killing of two special police officers. Initial reports indicate that the officers may have been accidentally shot by Army personnel during a hunting operation. The BJP has dismissed these allegations, claiming they tarnish the integrity of the security forces. Mumbai physics forum hosts online lecture by Pak N-scientist. Mumbai recently held an online event to honor the birth centenary of Nobel laureate Abdus Salam. Eminent scientist Pervez Amirali Hoodbhoy delivered a lecture discussing Salam's contributions to physics and his life. Hoodbhoy highlighted Salam's significance as a symbol of goodwill between India and Pakistan. He mentioned Salam's lack of recognition in Pakistan due to his Ahmadiyya sect affiliation, affecting youth role models. Kashmir film fraternity trains guns on Bollywood's 'AK-47 and skullcap' stereotype, seeks own industry. Kashmiri filmmakers are advocating for a shift towards regional cinema to enhance authentic storytelling and representation. They argue that Bollywood often reinforces stereotypes that misrepresent life in J and K. The current film policy is criticized for not adequately supporting local productions while favoring external filmmakers. Actors and directors are calling for collaboration among regional artists to develop a unique Kashmiri film industry, signaling a significant movement towards self-identity and cultural expression. Criminal killed in 5th 'encounter' in West Bengal since May. A history-sheeter in Bengal, who had allegedly shot and injured a constable on Nov 13, was killed by police Sunday, the fifth such "encounter death" in the state since BJP came to office in May. CRPF men in anti-Naxal ops diverted to Manipur. CRPF has withdrawn a battalion comprising more than 1,000 personnel from the anti Shah hits back at Rahul, says he's defaming India at global platforms. Union home minister Amit Shah Sunday accused leader of the opposition Rahul Gandhi of attempting to tarnish India's image on an international platform, referring to his remarks at the Bharat Summit 2026 in Hyderabad. Punjab BJP forms manifesto, 'chargesheet' committees; Raghav Chadha, Harbhajan Singh among members. Punjab BJP president Kewal Singh Dhillon has created two vital committees. One will meticulously draft the party manifesto, while the other focuses on compiling a detailed chargesheet. Senior leaders Avinash Rai Khanna and Sunil Jakhar are at the helm, supported by a diverse range of experts, showcasing the party's commitment to thorough preparation for a strategic electoral campaign. India bucks trend, 38 institutions up in QS sustainability study. India was only one of the world's five most represented systems to record more universities rising than falling in QS World University Rankings: Sustainability 2027. 'Well-planned conspiracy': BJP refutes reports of 209-candidate list for upcoming UP elections. The Bharatiya Janata Party's Uttar Pradesh unit has refuted claims regarding a supposed list of 209 candidates. Officials described these reports as false and part of a larger scheme. They cautioned party members against believing in unverified media stories. Additionally, they clarified that the assembly election candidate selection process has yet to commence, highlighting the importance of a methodical and unified approach to such decisions. Kishtwar BJP leader questions Shagun Parihar's mosque claim, Muslim body seeks public apology. Kishtwar BJP leader Jahanzaib Sirwal on Sunday questioned party MLA Shagun Parihar's claim that announcements were made from a mosque before two SPOs were killed in Kishtwar's Dachhan area, calling the allegation "deeply unfortunate and factually unsubstantiated".

transcript.title: Around the world
transcript.text: And finally, here is what is happening around the world. South Korea's top scorer in tax accountancy exam admits cheating. Han Won-seok, 34, confessed to using a hidden camera and AI to get a near-perfect mark on the significant test. Czechs rally against plan to switch funding of public media. Protesters say the move will stifle media freedom, while the government insists broadcasters need to cut costs. Police ban protests near 10 schools and five universities in Paris. The order will be in place from 16 to 20 November, Paris police chief Patrice Faure says. Three men sentenced to death in Jordan over fatal church mass shooting. The attack on funeral at a Greek Orthodox church killed nine and injured 34 others last month. 'Can you believe it?': SpaceX catches part of its Starship rocket on return to Earth. SpaceX has performed the historic catch using mechanical arms nicknamed "chopsticks".

transcript.title: Sign-off
transcript.text: That is your briefing. Stay sharp, and have a strong day.
